title: Thread panel: comment selection and per-comment actions
design:
## Requirements (IMMUTABLE)
- j/k keymaps in the panel buffer jump between comments (to each comment's first line); arrow keys move freely within the buffer
- CursorMoved autocmd on panel buffer tracks which comment the cursor is in and updates selection highlight accordingly
- Panel opens unfocused (cursor stays in editor); user uses standard <C-w>p to move cursor into panel; q/Esc close panel (existing behavior)
- No setup() config option for focus behavior
- Selection highlight (NitThreadSelected) coexists with zebra-striping: selection extmarks at priority 300, zebra at priority 200
- Context-sensitive action menu (C-a) shows: always q=Quote reply; own non-optimistic comment adds e=Edit comment; comment with ```suggestion block adds a=Apply suggestion; r=Resolve/Unresolve always present
- Quote reply opens (or focuses) reply_input with GitHub-style '> @author: text\n\n' prefilled and cursor at bottom
- Edit comment opens a reply_input-style split pre-filled with comment.body; on C-s submits via updatePullRequestReviewComment GraphQL mutation + optimistic update
- Apply suggestion: parses ```suggestion block from comment.body, replaces lines in the file buffer via nvim_buf_set_lines using thread.path/start_line/line; no API call
- No delete comment action (out of scope)
- No editing of optimistic comments (comment._optimistic_id must be nil)

## Success Criteria (MUST ALL BE TRUE)
- [ ] j/k navigate between comments with cursor moving to comment start line
- [ ] CursorMoved resolves selection and applies NitThreadSelected highlight
- [ ] Selection highlight visible and distinct while zebra-stripes remain visible
- [ ] <C-w>p from editor moves cursor to panel; j/k work; q closes
- [ ] Action menu shows correct context-sensitive items per comment
- [ ] Quote reply prefills reply_input with formatted quote
- [ ] Edit comment flow: pre-fills body, submits mutation, optimistic update applied
- [ ] Apply suggestion replaces correct lines in file buffer without API call
- [ ] All tests passing
- [ ] Pre-commit hooks passing

## Anti-Patterns (FORBIDDEN)
- ❌ NO nui.Menu for per-comment actions (it is popup-only, cannot embed in Split; use existing thread_menu.lua pattern)
- ❌ NO duplicate line-counting logic (format_thread is the single source of truth for line layout; ranges must come from it, not a parallel function)
- ❌ NO editing optimistic comments (no node ID yet; guard: comment._optimistic_id must be nil before showing edit action)
- ❌ NO delete comment action (out of scope per REQUIREMENTS.md)
- ❌ NO state-layer selection state (selection is display-local; do not add selected_comment_id to state/observers)
- ❌ NO config option for focus behavior (always opens unfocused; <C-w>p is the entry point)
- ❌ NO full upfront task tree (create tasks iteratively as each one completes)

## Approach
Extend format_thread to return comment_ranges (Nit.Display.CommentRange[]) alongside the existing lines and author_indices. This keeps format_thread as the single source of truth for panel layout.

Add module-level selected_comment_idx and comment_ranges state to thread_panel.lua. Register a CursorMoved autocmd on the panel buffer that resolves selection and drives a dedicated selection namespace (selection_ns, priority 300). j/k keymaps advance/retreat the selection and move the cursor.

The action menu (thread_menu.lua) gains an optional comment parameter. Context-sensitive items are computed from viewer_login, comment._optimistic_id, and comment.body content. Quote reply, edit comment, and apply suggestion are implemented as standalone functions in thread_panel.lua called from the menu.

## Architecture
- lua/nit/display/thread_panel.lua — format_thread signature change; new module state; CursorMoved autocmd; j/k keymaps; select_comment(), redraw_selection(), find_comment_at_line(); quote_reply(); edit_comment(); apply_suggestion()
- lua/nit/display/thread_menu.lua — extend open() with optional comment param; context-sensitive item list
- lua/nit/ui/highlights.lua — add NitThreadSelected highlight group
- lua/nit/api/types.lua — add Nit.Display.CommentRange class annotation (or thread_panel.lua local annotation)
- tests/display/thread_panel_spec.lua — format_thread range tests, selection tracking tests
- tests/display/thread_menu_spec.lua — context-sensitive item tests

## Design Rationale
### Problem
The thread panel displays comments but has no way to act on individual comments. Users cannot edit their own comments, quote-reply, or apply code suggestions from within the panel. Navigation between comments requires manual cursor movement with no visual feedback about which comment is 'active'.

### Research Findings
**Codebase:**
- thread_panel.lua:120-159 — format_thread returns (lines, author_indices); line-counting already sequential per comment, range tracking is a natural extension
- thread_panel.lua:396-411 — get_line_highlights uses author_indices to drive extmarks at priority 200; selection at 300 will overlay cleanly
- thread_panel.lua:322-340 — panel keymaps use panel:map(); j/k are currently unbound (free to override)
- thread_menu.lua:13-71 — open(thread, callbacks) pattern with parallel lines/actions tables; extensible to comment context
- manager.lua:99-117 — CursorMoved pattern on source buffer; same pattern applies to panel buffer
- highlights.lua:34-83 — NitThreadComment/Alt defined with blend; NitThreadSelected follows same pattern

### Approaches Considered

#### 1. Extend format_thread return value ✓

**What it is:** format_thread already iterates comments sequentially and counts lines. Extending it to emit CommentRange[] alongside its existing return values adds no duplication and keeps layout logic in one place.

**Investigation:**
- Reviewed format_thread:120-159 — iterates thread.comments, tracks separator + author + body lines; adding range tracking is 4 lines of bookkeeping
- Checked callers of format_thread — all destructure (lines, author_indices); adding third return value is backward-compatible with _ discard

**Pros:**
- No duplication of line-counting logic
- format_thread remains single source of truth
- Callers that don't need ranges ignore the third value

**Cons:**
- format_thread returns three values instead of two (minor)

**Chosen because:** Eliminates duplication risk; consistent with how get_line_highlights consumes author_indices from the same function.

#### 2. Separate get_comment_ranges() function ❌

**What it is:** A parallel function that replicates format_thread's line-counting to produce ranges independently.

**Why we looked at this:** Avoids changing format_thread's signature.

**Investigation:**
- format_thread has interleaved separator/author/body line counting; duplicating this is ~40 lines of coupled logic
- Any future format_thread change (e.g. new line type) requires updating both functions

**Pros:**
- format_thread signature unchanged

**Cons:**
- DRY violation: two functions counting the same lines in the same way
- Brittle: format changes break ranges silently

**⚠️ REJECTED BECAUSE:** Duplication is worse than a three-value return.

**🚫 DO NOT REVISIT UNLESS:** format_thread becomes so complex that a separate layout pass is warranted.

#### 3. State-driven selection via observers ❌

**What it is:** Add selected_comment_id to state module, drive highlight reactively via observers subscription.

**Why we looked at this:** Selection visible from anywhere in plugin; reactive to state changes.

**Investigation:**
- Selection is purely a display concern; nothing outside thread_panel.lua needs to know which comment is selected
- Observer overhead for display-local state is unnecessary coupling

**Pros:**
- Selection globally accessible

**Cons:**
- Overengineered: selection is display-local
- Adds unnecessary state complexity
- Couples display to state module

**⚠️ REJECTED BECAUSE:** Violates YAGNI; selection is not needed outside the display layer.

**🚫 DO NOT REVISIT UNLESS:** Another display component (e.g. file panel) needs to react to selected comment.

### Scope Boundaries
**In scope:**
- j/k comment navigation + CursorMoved selection
- NitThreadSelected highlight group
- Context-sensitive action menu (extend thread_menu.lua)
- Quote reply into reply_input
- Edit own comment (non-optimistic) via updatePullRequestReviewComment
- Apply suggestion (local buffer edit, no API)

**Out of scope (deferred/never):**
- Delete comment (REQUIREMENTS.md: never)
- Editing optimistic comments (no node ID)
- Multi-selection (not requested)
- Comment bookmarking/jumping from editor (separate feature)

### Open Questions
- Quote truncation: truncate at 72 chars or include full body in quote? (decide during implementation)
- Edit window: reuse reply_input module or duplicate pattern? (prefer reuse if API allows)
- Suggestion parser: handle multi-hunk suggestions? (defer; single-hunk first)

## Design Discovery (Reference Context)

> Preserved Q&A and research from brainstorming for task creation and obstacle handling.

### Key Decisions Made

| Question | User Answer | Implication |
|----------|-------------|-------------|
| Focus model: j/k when unfocused? | Focus first (standard <C-w>p), then j/k navigate | Panel is passive when unfocused; no global keybindings needed |
| Quote reply destination? | Prefill reply_input with '> @author: text\n\n' | quote_reply() must open/focus reply_input and insert content |
| Apply suggestion trigger? | Action menu only (context-sensitive) | No dedicated keybinding for apply suggestion |
| Focus toggle key? | Standard <C-w>p / q-Esc to leave | No custom Tab binding; q/Esc close panel (existing behavior preserved) |
| Setup() config for focus? | No, default behavior only | No new setup() options needed |

### Research Deep-Dives

#### Thread panel line layout
**Question explored:** How does format_thread count lines, and can ranges be derived from it?
**Sources consulted:**
- thread_panel.lua:120-159 — format_thread source
- thread_panel.lua:396-411 — get_line_highlights consuming author_indices

**Findings:**
- format_thread iterates comments, inserts separator (except first), author line, blank, body lines
- Line counts are sequential and deterministic; adding a range tracker is trivial
- get_line_highlights already consumes (lines, author_indices) from format_thread; CommentRange[] follows the same pattern

**Conclusion:** Extend format_thread return — cleanest, no duplication

#### Existing keybinding gaps
**Question explored:** Are j/k bound in the panel? Any conflicts?
**Sources consulted:**
- thread_panel.lua:322-340 — keybinding setup

**Findings:**
- j/k are NOT currently bound in the panel buffer; they perform default Neovim line movement
- Overriding j/k with comment-jump behavior is safe and expected

**Conclusion:** j/k free to bind for comment navigation

#### Selection highlight priority
**Question explored:** Will a selection highlight at priority 300 overlay zebra stripes correctly?
**Sources consulted:**
- thread_panel.lua:437-458 — extmark application at priority 200

**Findings:**
- Neovim extmark priority: higher number wins for line_hl_group
- Selection at 300 will override zebra at 200 on selected lines
- Adjacent unselected lines retain their zebra coloring

**Conclusion:** Priority 300 for NitThreadSelected is correct

### Dead-End Paths

#### Separate get_comment_ranges() function
**Why explored:** Avoids changing format_thread's two-value return
**Investigation:** Counted ~40 lines of duplicated line-counting logic; identified brittleness risk
**Why abandoned:** DRY violation worse than three-value return

#### State-driven selection
**Why explored:** Global accessibility of selected comment
**Investigation:** No other module needs selected comment; observer overhead unjustified
**Why abandoned:** YAGNI; display-local concern

### Open Concerns Raised
- None raised during brainstorming

title: Bug: format_relative_time double-subtracts UTC offset, showing wrong age
description: GitHub timestamps are UTC. The function parses them as local time (parsed_as_local), then computes utc_offset = now - os.time(utc_table). It then subtracts utc_offset when it should add it. This double-subtracts the offset, making recent comments look older by 2× the timezone offset.
close_reason: Fixed: changed parsed_utc = parsed_as_local - utc_offset to + utc_offset in format_relative_time. Root cause was double-subtraction of timezone offset (parsed UTC string as local time, then subtracted offset again instead of adding). Regression test added. 478/478 tests pass.

title: Bug: resolved threads excluded from thread panel
description: manager.lua filter_displayable has 'and not thread.isResolved' condition that prevents resolved threads from being displayed in the thread panel. Resolved threads should be viewable — the user explicitly opened that thread. Fix: remove the isResolved exclusion from filter_displayable in lua/nit/display/manager.lua.
close_reason: Fixed in working tree: isResolved condition removed from filter_displayable in manager.lua

title: Feature: comment reactions (add, remove, display)
description: Users cannot react to individual comments from within the thread panel. WORKFLOW.md mentions reactions in the thread display but they are not fetched, stored, or rendered. The addReaction/removeReaction GraphQL mutations require a comment node ID which the current review threads query does not fetch.
design:
## Requirements (IMMUTABLE)
- Reactions are fetched for review thread comments via extended REVIEW_THREADS_QUERY (reactionGroups: content, viewerHasReacted, reactors.totalCount; plus node id field)
- Nit.Api.Comment gains node_id (string, GraphQL global ID) and reactions (ReactionGroup[]) fields
- Nit.Api.ReactionGroup: { content: string, count: integer, viewer_has_reacted: boolean }
- mutations.lua exposes add_reaction(opts, callback) and remove_reaction(opts, callback) using addReaction/removeReaction GraphQL mutations
- orchestration.toggle_reaction(opts) determines add vs remove from current viewer_has_reacted state, applies optimistic update, queues API call, restores snapshot on failure
- format_thread() renders a compact reaction summary line below comments that have reactions (e.g. '👍 2  ❤️ 1') using the 8 GitHub reaction emojis
- Viewer's own reactions are visually distinct (NitThreadReactionOwn highlight group)
- A reaction picker popup lists all 8 reactions with number hotkeys 1-8; viewer's existing reactions marked with ✓; selecting toggles add/remove
- Thread menu (C-a) gains a 'React' entry that opens the reaction picker for the selected comment
- Thread menu comment context comes from nit.nvim-0mh comment selection

## Success Criteria (MUST ALL BE TRUE)
- [ ] REVIEW_THREADS_QUERY fetches id and reactionGroups for comment nodes
- [ ] Nit.Api.Comment has node_id and reactions fields with LuaCATS annotations
- [ ] add_reaction() and remove_reaction() in mutations.lua follow existing mutation pattern
- [ ] toggle_reaction() in orchestration applies optimistic update and restores on failure
- [ ] Reaction summary lines render below comments with reactions in the thread panel
- [ ] Reaction picker popup opens from thread menu, shows viewer reaction state
- [ ] Selecting a marked (✓) reaction removes it; selecting unmarked adds it
- [ ] All tests passing
- [ ] Pre-commit hooks passing

## Anti-Patterns (FORBIDDEN)
- ❌ NO using databaseId as subjectId for mutations (security/correctness: addReaction requires GraphQL global node ID, not integer databaseId)
- ❌ NO separate add/remove menu entries (UX: single React entry with picker and clear ✓ state is the agreed design)
- ❌ NO reaction state outside the comment object (consistency: reactions live on Nit.Api.Comment, not separate state module)
- ❌ NO full upfront task tree (process: create tasks iteratively as each completes)
- ❌ NO fetching reactions for PR-level issue comments via REST workaround (consistency: GraphQL reactionGroups is the correct approach)

## Approach
Extend the GraphQL query and type system first (API layer is independent of nit.nvim-0mh). Then add mutations and orchestration. Display rendering in format_thread can also proceed independently. The reaction picker popup and thread menu integration require nit.nvim-0mh to provide the selected comment context.

## Architecture
- lua/nit/api/types.lua — Add ReactionGroup class, ReactionContent alias; extend Comment with node_id and reactions
- lua/nit/api/comments.lua — Extend REVIEW_THREADS_QUERY + normalize_threads()
- lua/nit/api/pr.lua — Update normalize_reactions() to produce ReactionGroup[]
- lua/nit/api/mutations.lua — Add add_reaction(), remove_reaction()
- lua/nit/orchestration/init.lua — Add toggle_reaction()
- lua/nit/display/thread_panel.lua — Reaction summary rendering in format_thread()
- lua/nit/ui/highlights.lua — Add NitThreadReaction, NitThreadReactionOwn
- lua/nit/display/reaction_picker.lua — New reaction picker popup
- lua/nit/display/thread_menu.lua — Add React entry (depends on nit.nvim-0mh)

## Design Rationale
### Problem
Thread panel shows comments but users cannot express reactions. WORKFLOW.md specifies reactions as part of the thread display. The current Nit.Api.Comment type lacks node_id (needed for mutations) and reactions fields. No mutations exist for reactions.

### Research Findings
**Codebase:**
- lua/nit/api/comments.lua:26-36 — REVIEW_THREADS_QUERY comment nodes fetch databaseId but not id or reactionGroups
- lua/nit/api/types.lua:66-76 — Nit.Api.Comment has no node_id or reactions fields
- lua/nit/api/mutations.lua:9-42 — Existing mutation pattern: GraphQL string + parse_graphql_response() helper
- lua/nit/orchestration/init.lua:115-162 — toggle_resolved() is the pattern for toggle_reaction() (optimistic + queue + snapshot)
- lua/nit/display/thread_panel.lua:120-159 — format_thread() iterates comments sequentially; reaction line appended after body lines
- lua/nit/display/thread_menu.lua:13-71 — lines + parallel actions tables; hotkey dispatch + CR cursor dispatch
- nit.nvim-0mh epic — provides comment parameter to thread_menu.open() for per-comment targeting

### Approaches Considered

#### 1. GraphQL reactionGroups on comment nodes ✓
Extend REVIEW_THREADS_QUERY to include reactionGroups with viewerHasReacted. Single query fetches everything needed.
**Chosen because:** Consistent with existing GraphQL-first approach; viewerHasReacted from server is authoritative.

#### 2. REST endpoint for reactions ❌
Use gh api /repos/.../pulls/comments/:id/reactions.
**Why explored:** REST endpoints exist for reactions.
**⚠️ REJECTED BECAUSE:** Extra API call per comment; no viewerHasReacted field; inconsistent with GraphQL-first pattern.
**🚫 DO NOT REVISIT UNLESS:** GraphQL reactionGroups proves unreliable.

### Scope Boundaries
**In scope:** Review thread comment reactions (fetch + display + add + remove). PR-level IssueComment type updated to use ReactionGroup[].
**Out of scope:** Displaying PR-level comments (no display surface yet). Reaction counts on comment popup.

## Design Discovery

### Key Decisions Made
| Question | User Answer | Implication |
|----------|-------------|-------------|
| Comment types | Both review threads and PR-level | API mutations work for both; display for thread panel only |
| UX trigger | Thread menu (C-a) → React entry | Extends existing thread_menu pattern |
| Toggle vs separate | Single React entry, clear visual state | Picker shows ✓ on viewer reactions |
| Display reactions | Yes, compact summary line | Reaction line appended in format_thread() |
| Comment targeting | Aligns with nit.nvim-0mh | Epic depends on comment selection epic |

title: v1.1: Thread interactions
design:
## Requirements (IMMUTABLE)
- Reply input: user submits replies with C-s or <CR>; toggle resolve with C-r; optimistic update applied immediately; mutation failure reverts state with vim.notify error
- Mutation queue: all mutations spaced ≥1100ms to avoid GitHub secondary rate limit; failures surface actionable notifications; queue testable end-to-end
- Context menu: cursor-aware action menu via require('nit').menu(); items absent (not greyed) when irrelevant to cursor position; hotkeys right-aligned
- Command wiring: require('nit') exposes menu(), next_comment(), prev_comment(); :Nit subcommands with tab completion; plugin registers no automatic keybindings
- Comment navigation: j/k in panel jump between comments; CursorMoved drives NitThreadSelected highlight (priority 300, coexists with zebra at 200)
- Per-comment actions (C-a): quote reply prefills reply_input with '> \@author: text\n\n'; edit own non-optimistic comment pre-fills body, submits via updatePullRequestReviewComment; apply suggestion replaces lines in file buffer without API call; resolve/unresolve always available
- Reply input line wrapping must not leak hard breaks to the GitHub API
- No delete comment action (out of scope per REQUIREMENTS.md)

## Success Criteria (MUST ALL BE TRUE)
- [ ] Reply submits optimistically; reverts with notification on failure
- [ ] Rapid mutations spaced ≥1100ms; secondary rate limit not triggerable in normal use
- [ ] Context menu items appear/absent correctly per cursor position (no disabled/greyed items)
- [ ] :Nit menu/next/prev wired and appear in :Nit tab completion
- [ ] j/k navigate between comments; NitThreadSelected highlight visible and distinct from zebra
- [ ] Quote reply, edit comment, apply suggestion, resolve/unresolve work for appropriate comment types
- [ ] Hard line wrapping stripped before GitHub API submission
- [ ] All tests passing
- [ ] Pre-commit hooks passing

## Anti-Patterns (FORBIDDEN)
- ❌ NO automatic keybindings registered by plugin (user maps everything in their own config)
- ❌ NO config options for v1.1 UI behaviors (hardcode sensible defaults)
- ❌ NO greyed-out or disabled menu items (absent items preferred)
- ❌ NO delete comment action (REQUIREMENTS.md: out of scope)
- ❌ NO editing optimistic comments (guard: comment._optimistic_id must be nil)
- ❌ NO state-layer selection state (selection is display-local to thread_panel.lua)
- ❌ NO full upfront task tree (create tasks iteratively via executing-plans)

## Approach
v1.1 delivers end-to-end thread interactivity. Work proceeds in dependency order: reply input (Phase 12) unblocks mutation queue (Phase 13) and comment selection epic; context menu (Phase 14) follows mutation queue; command wiring (Phase 15) closes out the public API surface.

Bugs (11y, dj7, fwn) are fixed as part of Phase 12 since they all affect the reply input. Thread menu hotkey alignment (fx6) is fixed as part of Phase 14 context menu work.

## Architecture
- lua/nit/display/thread_panel.lua — reply input, comment navigation, selection highlight, per-comment action dispatch
- lua/nit/display/thread_menu.lua — context-sensitive menu with right-aligned hotkeys
- lua/nit/api/mutations.lua — rate-limited mutation queue (≥1100ms spacing)
- lua/nit/commands.lua — :Nit subcommand wiring
- lua/nit/init.lua — public Lua API: menu(), next_comment(), prev_comment()
- tests/display/thread_panel_spec.lua — reply input, navigation, selection tests
- tests/api/mutations_spec.lua — queue rate-limiting tests

title: Task 1: Extend format_thread to return CommentRange[]
design:
## Goal
Extend format_thread() to return a third value: Nit.Display.CommentRange[] mapping each comment to its 1-based start/end lines in the panel buffer. This is the foundational data structure for all selection-tracking work in subsequent tasks.

## Effort estimate
2-4 hours

## Implementation

1. Study existing code
   - lua/nit/display/thread_panel.lua:120-159 — format_thread. Read carefully: separator line is inserted at line 127 (`table.insert(lines, '')`) ONLY for i > 1, BEFORE the author line. This means start_line must be captured AFTER the separator insert. Author line is always the first line of a comment's range.
   - lua/nit/display/thread_panel.lua:427 — only internal caller: `local lines, author_indices = M.format_thread(thread)` in M.update()
   - tests/display/thread_panel_spec.lua:6-200 — existing format_thread test structure; note comment fixtures at lines 9-16 have no `id` field (comment.id will be nil for those — acceptable since existing tests don't check ranges)

2. Write tests first (TDD)
   Test file: tests/display/thread_panel_spec.lua, inside `describe('format_thread', ...)`.

   **Required test cases:**

   a. Zero comments → ranges = {} (empty table)
      ```lua
      it('returns empty ranges for thread with no comments', function()
        local thread = { comments = {} }
        local _, _, ranges = thread_panel.format_thread(thread)
        assert.are.same({}, ranges)
      end)
      ```

   b. Single comment, single-line body
      ```lua
      it('returns correct range for single comment', function()
        local thread = { comments = {
          { id = 'c1', author = { login = 'alice' }, body = 'hello', createdAt = '2026-01-01T00:00:00Z' }
        } }
        local lines, _, ranges = thread_panel.format_thread(thread)
        -- lines: [author_line, '', ' hello'] = 3 lines
        assert.are.equal(1, #ranges)
        assert.are.equal('c1', ranges[1].comment_id)
        assert.are.equal(1, ranges[1].start_line)   -- author line
        assert.are.equal(#lines, ranges[1].end_line) -- last body line
        assert.are.equal(1, ranges[1].comment_index)
      end)
      ```

   c. Two comments — separator is NOT in either range (there is a gap)
      ```lua
      it('separator lines between comments are not in any range', function()
        local thread = { comments = {
          { id = 'c1', author = { login = 'alice' }, body = 'A', createdAt = '2026-01-01T00:00:00Z' },
          { id = 'c2', author = { login = 'bob' },   body = 'B', createdAt = '2026-01-02T00:00:00Z' },
        } }
        local _, _, ranges = thread_panel.format_thread(thread)
        assert.are.equal(2, #ranges)
        -- Comment 1: lines 1-3 (author, blank, body)
        assert.are.equal(1, ranges[1].start_line)
        assert.are.equal(3, ranges[1].end_line)
        -- Separator: line 4 (blank) — NOT in any range
        -- Comment 2: starts at line 5 (author), not line 4 (separator)
        assert.are.equal(5, ranges[2].start_line)
        assert.are.equal(7, ranges[2].end_line)
        -- Gap exists: ranges[1].end_line + 2 == ranges[2].start_line
        assert.are.equal(ranges[1].end_line + 2, ranges[2].start_line)
      end)
      ```

   d. Multiline body — end_line accounts for all body lines
      ```lua
      it('end_line covers all body lines for multiline body', function()
        local thread = { comments = {
          { id = 'c1', author = { login = 'alice' }, body = 'line1\nline2\nline3', createdAt = '2026-01-01T00:00:00Z' }
        } }
        local _, _, ranges = thread_panel.format_thread(thread)
        -- lines: [author, blank, ' line1', ' line2', ' line3'] = 5 lines
        assert.are.equal(5, ranges[1].end_line)
      end)
      ```

   e. comment_id and comment_index are correct for all comments
      ```lua
      it('comment_id and comment_index match thread.comments for each range', function()
        local thread = { comments = {
          { id = 'id-1', author = { login = 'a' }, body = 'x', createdAt = '2026-01-01T00:00:00Z' },
          { id = 'id-2', author = { login = 'b' }, body = 'y', createdAt = '2026-01-02T00:00:00Z' },
          { id = 'id-3', author = { login = 'c' }, body = 'z', createdAt = '2026-01-03T00:00:00Z' },
        } }
        local _, _, ranges = thread_panel.format_thread(thread)
        assert.are.equal(3, #ranges)
        assert.are.equal('id-1', ranges[1].comment_id)
        assert.are.equal(1, ranges[1].comment_index)
        assert.are.equal('id-2', ranges[2].comment_id)
        assert.are.equal(2, ranges[2].comment_index)
        assert.are.equal('id-3', ranges[3].comment_id)
        assert.are.equal(3, ranges[3].comment_index)
      end)
      ```

3. Implementation checklist
   - [ ] lua/nit/display/thread_panel.lua:119 — Add LuaCATS annotation for Nit.Display.CommentRange as a module-local type (above the function):
     ```lua
     ---@class Nit.Display.CommentRange
     ---@field comment_id string Node ID from Nit.Api.Comment
     ---@field start_line integer 1-based line number of author header (AFTER separator, not the separator itself)
     ---@field end_line integer 1-based inclusive last line of comment body
     ---@field comment_index integer 1-based position in thread.comments
     ```
   - [ ] lua/nit/display/thread_panel.lua:119 — Update ---@return annotation on format_thread:
     ```lua
     ---@return string[], table<integer, true>, Nit.Display.CommentRange[]
     ```
   - [ ] lua/nit/display/thread_panel.lua:120 — In format_thread body, add `local ranges = {}` after `local author_indices = {}`
   - [ ] lua/nit/display/thread_panel.lua:126-128 — Capture start_line AFTER inserting separator:
     ```lua
     if i > 1 then
       table.insert(lines, '')  -- separator: NOT part of this comment's range
     end
     local start_line = #lines + 1  -- points to author line (inserted next)
     ```
   - [ ] lua/nit/display/thread_panel.lua:155 — After the body_lines loop, record the range:
     ```lua
     table.insert(ranges, {
       comment_id = comment.id,
       start_line = start_line,
       end_line = #lines,
       comment_index = i,
     })
     ```
   - [ ] lua/nit/display/thread_panel.lua:158 — Update return statement:
     ```lua
     return lines, author_indices, ranges
     ```
   - [ ] lua/nit/display/thread_panel.lua:427 — Update M.update() caller (only internal caller):
     ```lua
     local lines, author_indices, _ = M.format_thread(thread)
     ```
   - [ ] tests/display/thread_panel_spec.lua — Add the 5 test cases above inside the existing `describe('format_thread', ...)` block

## Success Criteria
- [ ] format_thread returns three values: lines, author_indices, comment_ranges
- [ ] Zero-comment thread: ranges = {}
- [ ] Single-comment thread: ranges[1].start_line = 1, end_line = correct last line
- [ ] Two-comment thread: separator line is a gap — ranges[1].end_line + 2 == ranges[2].start_line
- [ ] comment_id and comment_index correct for 3-comment thread
- [ ] All 5 new range tests pass
- [ ] All existing format_thread tests still pass (caller at line 427 uses _ for third value)
- [ ] `make test` passes
- [ ] `make typecheck` passes
- [ ] Pre-commit hooks passing

## Anti-Patterns (FORBIDDEN)
- ❌ NO capturing start_line BEFORE the separator insert (start_line must be the author line, not the blank separator; check: `start_line = #lines + 1` placed AFTER `if i > 1 then table.insert(lines, '') end`)
- ❌ NO including separator lines in any range (separator is a visual gap, never owned by a comment)
- ❌ NO contiguous ranges (ranges intentionally have gaps at separator lines; a test asserting contiguity is wrong)
- ❌ NO duplicate line-counting function (ranges come from format_thread only)
- ❌ NO changing existing tests to add `id` fields (existing tests don't test ranges; their comment.id will be nil which is fine for them)
- ❌ NO globals; all new variables local to format_thread body

## Key Considerations (SRE REVIEW)

**Separator line ownership:**
- format_thread inserts a blank `''` line at the start of each comment with i > 1 (line 127)
- This separator is BEFORE the author line, so `start_line` must be captured AFTER inserting it
- Separator lines are gaps in the range table: `find_comment_at_line(separator_line, ranges)` should return nil in Task 3
- Test case (c) above verifies this explicitly with hardcoded expected values

**Multiline body with trailing newline:**
- `vim.split('hello\nworld\n', '\n', { plain = true })` → `{ 'hello', 'world', '' }` (3 elements, last empty)
- Empty body_line gets `table.insert(lines, '')` (not `' '`) at line 150-152
- end_line will correctly include this trailing empty line — no special handling needed

**Zero-comment thread:**
- `ipairs({})` never executes; `ranges = {}` returned — correct behavior
- Must be tested explicitly to guard against off-by-one bugs on the loop setup

**Existing callers:**
- Only one internal caller: M.update() at line 427 — update it with `_` for third return value
- External callers (e.g. tests) that use `local lines, author_indices = format_thread(...)` are unaffected (Lua silently discards extra return values)

For author lines in even comments, use NitThreadCommentAlt instead of CursorLine. Odd comments keep existing styling.

description: The REVIEW_THREADS_QUERY does not fetch node id or reactionGroups for comments. Nit.Api.Comment has no node_id or reactions fields. Without these, reaction mutations cannot be called and reactions cannot be displayed.

3. Query extension (lua/nit/api/comments.lua)

   - Add M.add_reaction(opts, callback) following reply_to_thread() pattern

title: Commit-by-commit review flow
description: Users review PRs commit by commit using codediff.nvim for diff display. nit.nvim must integrate with that flow to enable leaving and viewing review comments scoped to a specific commit.
design:
## Requirements (IMMUTABLE)
- nit.nvim detects when the active buffer is a codediff.nvim commit diff buffer and derives commit context (SHA, file path, line) from it
- From a commit diff buffer, user can open a reply/comment input and leave a PR review comment scoped to that commit position (correct commit SHA + file + line sent to GitHub API)
- Thread panel shows comments for the current commit + file context when viewing a commit diff (not the full PR thread list)
- All existing :Nit commands and require('nit') API work the same in commit diff buffers — no separate commands
- nit.nvim uses codediff.nvim's public API only; no coupling to internals or private buffer vars

## Success Criteria (MUST ALL BE TRUE)
- [ ] Opening a comment from a codediff.nvim buffer submits it to GitHub with the correct commit SHA, file, and line
- [ ] Thread panel shows commit-scoped comments when viewing a commit diff
- [ ] Switching back to the PR diff view shows PR-scoped comments (not commit-scoped)
- [ ] All existing PR-level review flows continue to work unchanged
- [ ] All tests passing
- [ ] Pre-commit hooks passing

## Anti-Patterns (FORBIDDEN)
- ❌ NO reimplementing diff viewing (codediff.nvim owns that; nit.nvim is the review layer only)
- ❌ NO coupling to codediff.nvim internals — use public API only (once researched)
- ❌ NO separate :Nit commands for commit context (same commands, context-aware behavior)
- ❌ NO full upfront task tree (create tasks iteratively as each one completes)

## Approach
nit.nvim acts as the review layer on top of codediff.nvim's diff display. The integration point is detecting the current buffer's context: when it's a codediff.nvim buffer, extract commit SHA + file + line; when it's a normal PR diff buffer, use the existing PR diff position logic.

GitHub PR review comments can be scoped to a commit by including the commit_id field in the API call. The core API change is making comment submission context-aware.

## Open Questions (resolve in Task 1)
- How does codediff.nvim expose commit SHA, file path, and line to other plugins?
- Is there an event/autocmd codediff fires when the viewed commit changes?
- How are codediff.nvim buffers identifiable (filetype, buffer var, name pattern)?
- Does codediff.nvim have a Lua API (require('codediff').get_context()) or only buffer-local vars?

description:
Create 5 rules in rules/tests/ that catch shorthand luassert assertions.

## Files to create

- rules/tests/no-shorthand-assert-same.yml    → catches assert.same($$$)

language: Lua
